hook_text: This salamander can regrow a lost leg. You can’t.
A mantis shrimp punches faster than you can blink.
Tardigrades can survive drying out for years. You’d last days.
Pigeons can find their way home from places they’ve never been.
A wood frog can spend winter partly frozen and hop away in spring.
Elephants may sense rumbles through their feet from kilometers away.
Your dog’s nose picks up smells you will never notice.
Hummingbirds can fly backwards. Try that with your arms.
An electric eel can make enough electricity to stun its prey.
Cuttlefish change color in a blink, yet they’re probably colorblind.
A gecko can walk up a window with no glue at all.
Bats can find insects in total darkness using sound.
Owls can turn their heads about 270 degrees. You manage around 90.
A dung beetle can steer by the Milky Way at night.
Some ants can carry many times their own body weight.
An octopus has three hearts, and its blood is blue.
A giraffe’s neck has seven bones. So does yours.
Starfish have no central brain and no blood.
A snail’s mouth can hold thousands of tiny teeth.
Koalas have fingerprints that look a lot like ours.
A cow has one stomach with four separate chambers.
That backward flamingo knee is really its ankle.
Horses have some of the largest eyes of any land mammal.
A slug breathes through a hole on the side of its body.
Sharks have no bones. Their skeleton is made of cartilage.
Snakes smell the air by flicking their forked tongues.
A chameleon’s eyes can look in two directions at once.
Cats have a third eyelid you rarely get to see.
T. rex arms were short, but fossils suggest they were heavily muscled.
A blue whale’s tongue alone can weigh as much as an elephant.
Scaled up to your size, a flea’s jump would clear a tall building.
Scaled to your size, some ants could lift a small car.
A newborn blue whale can weigh about as much as a pickup truck.
A red kangaroo can cover about 8 meters in one hop.
If you had a chameleon’s tongue, it could be up to twice your height.
A hummingbird’s heart can beat over 1,000 times a minute. Yours: about 70.
About a dozen tardigrades could line up along one grain of rice.
An elephant’s trunk can hold about 8 liters of water at once.
A sperm whale’s brain weighs about six times as much as yours.
Weight for weight, some spider silk is stronger than steel.
Tarsier eyes, scaled to your face, would each be grapefruit-sized.
An ostrich’s eye is bigger than its brain.
An emperor penguin can stand about as tall as a seven-year-old.
Some of the largest dinosaurs were about as long as three buses.
A megalodon tooth could be about as long as your whole hand.
When a predator gets close, a pufferfish puffs up into a spiky ball.
Threatened, a Virginia opossum may play dead for minutes at a time.
A hognose snake rolls over and plays dead when it feels threatened.
Some lizards drop their tails to escape, then grow new ones.
A skunk stamps its feet as a warning before it sprays.
Stick insects survive by looking exactly like twigs.
Octopuses can squirt ink to cover their escape.
A hedgehog rolls into a ball of spines when it’s scared.
Killdeer parents fake a broken wing to lead danger away from the nest.
Bombardier beetles spray a hot chemical mist to drive attackers off.
Some caterpillars have fake eyes that make them look like snakes.
A cat arches its back and puffs its fur to look bigger.
Sheep stay safer in a flock, where a predator struggles to pick one out.
Scientists still debate zebra stripes. One leading idea: fewer fly bites.
Ankylosaurus carried a bony club on the end of its tail.
It sleeps holding hands and keeps a rock in a skin pocket. Guess?
Clue one: it has no bones. Clue two: it tastes with its arms.
It lays eggs, has a duck-like bill, and it’s a mammal. Name it.
It can’t jump, and it’s the largest land animal alive. Guess?
It flies, but it’s a mammal, and it hangs upside down to sleep.
It’s the largest living bird, and it lays the largest eggs.
Its poop is cube-shaped. Its home is Australia. Who is it?
Its tongue is dark and up to about half a meter long. Guess?
It may have been North America’s most common bird. Now it’s extinct.
This beetle makes its own light and uses it to find a mate.
It has rectangular pupils and can climb surprisingly steep cliffs. Guess?
Sand temperature decides whether it hatches male or female. Name it.
Clue one: it’s pink. Clue two: it was born gray.
It’s a fish, it swims upright, and the dad gives birth.
It was a giant shark, and it vanished millions of years ago. Name it.
Your cat’s slow blink may be a friendly signal.
When your dog tilts its head, it may be trying to hear you better.
Your cat sees better in dim light than you do.
Your dog’s nose print is unique, like a fingerprint.
Your goldfish can learn to recognize feeding time.
Adult cats rarely meow at each other. The meowing is mostly for us.
Dogs go through sleep stages like ours, and they may dream.
Your rabbit’s teeth never stop growing.
Your cat’s whiskers help it judge whether it fits through a gap.
A hamster’s cheek pouches can stretch all the way back to its shoulders.
Many pet parrots can learn dozens of words.
Your cat kneads with its paws, a habit from kittenhood.
A chicken can tell many of its flockmates apart by their faces.
Your dog’s wagging tail doesn’t always mean happy.
Pigs can learn to come when their name is called.
Why it’s hard to be a sloth: digesting one leafy meal can take weeks.
Why it’s hard to be a mayfly: some adults live about a day.
Why it’s hard to be a panda: bamboo barely feeds you.
Why it’s hard to be a koala: eucalyptus leaves are low in energy.
Why it’s hard to be a hummingbird: you must eat almost constantly.
Emperor penguin dads guard the egg for about two months without eating.
Why it’s hard to be a salmon: you swim upriver to where you hatched.
Why it’s hard to be a giraffe: drinking water means doing the splits.
Why it’s hard to be a cicada: years underground for a few weeks above.
Why it’s hard to be a sea turtle hatchling: the race to the sea.
Why it’s hard to be a pig: you can barely sweat.
Why it was hard to be a woolly mammoth when the Ice Age ended.
Why it’s hard to be a bee: a summer worker lives about six weeks.
Why it’s hard to be a deep-sea fish: food rarely reaches you.
Why it’s hard to be a frog: your skin has to stay damp.
In the deep sea, anglerfish dangle a glowing lure in total darkness.
Woolly mammoths were still alive when the Great Pyramid was built.
Megalodon may have been about three times longer than a great white.
The dodo had never met humans, so it had no reason to run.
Many deep-sea animals make their own light. It’s called bioluminescence.
A giant squid’s eye can be about the size of a dinner plate.
Saber-toothed cats weren’t tigers. They weren’t even close relatives.
T. rex lived closer in time to you than to Stegosaurus.
Quetzalcoatlus had a wingspan about as wide as a small plane.
The vampire squid doesn’t drink blood. It eats drifting marine snow.
Trilobites roamed the seas for about 270 million years before vanishing.
The coelacanth was known from fossils, then a living one turned up in 1938.
Steller’s sea cow, up to about 8 meters long, was gone by 1768.
Below about 1,000 meters, the ocean is pitch dark all day long.
Archaeopteryx had feathers, wings, and a mouth full of teeth.
You’ve heard goldfish have three-second memories. Here’s the truth.
You’ve heard bulls hate the color red. They’re reacting to movement.
Ostriches don’t bury their heads in sand. Here’s what they’re actually doing.
Bats aren’t blind. Many see well and also use sound.
Harvestmen, the daddy longlegs, aren’t spiders and have no venom.
Chameleons don’t change color to match the background. Here’s why they do.
Lemmings don’t leap off cliffs in mass suicide.
Owls can’t spin their heads all the way around.
Camels don’t store water in their humps. It’s fat.
Elephants don’t drink through their trunks like straws.
Dogs don’t see only in black and white.
Pigs aren’t dirty. Mud is how they stay cool.
Flamingos aren’t born pink. Their color comes from food.
Megalodon isn’t hiding in the deep sea. It’s been extinct for millions of years.
Porcupines can’t shoot their quills. They only come loose on contact.
A cheetah can sprint at up to about 100 kilometers per hour.
A peregrine falcon’s dive can top 300 kilometers per hour.
The blue whale is the largest animal known to have ever lived.
A Greenland shark may live for 270 years or more.
The bee hummingbird is the smallest bird alive, about 5 to 6 centimeters long.
The Arctic tern’s yearly migration can cover around 70,000 kilometers.
Bowhead whales may live more than 200 years.
The sailfish is often called the fastest fish in the sea.
A giraffe is the tallest living animal, up to about 5.5 meters.
The ostrich lays the largest egg of any living bird.
The Komodo dragon is the largest living lizard.
A sperm whale has the largest brain of any known animal.
The African bush elephant is the largest land animal alive.
The goliath frog is the world’s largest frog, at up to about 3 kilograms.
The Etruscan shrew may be the lightest mammal, at about 2 grams.
